evidence.command: Read tracked README, build.sh, ProjectPaths, ServerManager, portable design, current Trinity checkout, and mesh gitlink
facts: The tracked README presents a three-command install but omits the required Trinity checkout, Bun dependencies, and companion runtime.
build.sh requires a sibling Trinity Queen package and bundles only libQueenUILib into trios.app.
The runtime companion is loaded from the BrowserOS source tree and requires an external Bun executable.
The mesh gitlink still points to local revision 27a76f21e3935b8ffe2e89e517a1f2821673c25f.
The local Trinity checkout still contains uncommitted Queen integration files.
The current app uses an ad-hoc signature rather than a notarized distribution identity.
No product code or install artifact was changed during the audit.

residual_risks: A double-click installer requires a self-contained signed bundle or an explicitly smaller core-only product.
A one-command source installer still requires publishing and pinning the cross-repository dependencies.
The user must choose the intended installation experience before the design can be implemented.
